data.title: Russia reports online attacks on voting system
data.description: MOSCOW - ⁠Russian ⁠authorities reported multiple attacks ​on voting systems and communication lines across ​the country on ‌Saturday, the second day of three days of voting in a parliamentary election.

data.title: Trump signs bill to impose sweeping Russia sanctions
data.description: WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump signed a bill on Friday authorising new sanctions designed to pressure Russia over its war in Ukraine, after Congress gave its approval after months of delay.

data.title: Western Australia beaches closed after fatal shark attack
data.description: ‌Several beaches along the coast of Western Australia, including in the state capital Perth, will remain closed until at least Sunday, authorities said, after a ​fatal ⁠shark attack at a popular beach in the city on Friday.

data.title: Death toll from attack at police HQ in Pakistan rises to 31
data.description: KOHAT, Pakistan - The death toll from an explosion and gun attack at a police headquarters in northern Pakistan rose to at least 31, including 16 police personnel, a senior police official told AFP on Saturday, with fighting ongoing.

data.title: Nigerian miners struggled to breathe in cell before 37 died: survivors
data.description: MINNA, Nigeria - Survivors of a Nigerian disaster in which 37 suspected illegal gold miners died while in the custody of a paramilitary civil defence group recounted their panic on Friday as they struggled to breathe inside the cell.

data.title: Drone owners rush to offload gear ahead of Beijing ban
data.description: BEIJING - Drone owners in Beijing flocked to designated buy-back sites this week, looking to sell their devices for as much as possible ahead of an impending citywide ban.

data.title: Helicopters battle wildfire threatening Ecuador's capital
data.description: QUITO - Ecuadoran firefighters backed by helicopters on Friday battled a major blaze on a hill overlooking the capital Quito that has led to the evacuation of dozens of people.

data.title: 'Pause' on overt repression in Venezuela, but reforms still needed: HRW
data.description: CARACAS - Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez has overseen a "pause" in the overt repression of opponents since taking office in January, Human Rights Watch (HRW) said Friday, 18 years after the organization was expelled from the country.

data.title: Trump claims 'infinite' Greenland security deal with Denmark
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump said Friday that he had struck a deal with Denmark to give Washington "permanent control" over Greenland's security that would bar Russia and China from setting up bases in the Arctic territory.

data.title: Nigeria miners struggled to breathe in cell before 37 died: survivors
data.description: MINNA (NIGERIA) - Survivors of a Nigerian disaster that saw 37 suspected illegal gold miners die while in the custody of a paramilitary civil defence group recounted their panic on Friday as they struggled to breathe inside the cell.

data.title: Cuba hit with seventh major blackout of the year
data.description: HAVANA - Cuba was plunged into its seventh massive blackout of the year on Friday, the energy ministry said, as fuel shortages bite on the US-blockaded island.

data.title: Trump says CNN, MS NOW, Politico banned from White House
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump said Friday he was banning news outlets CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, accusing them without specifics of reporting "fiction and lies."

data.title: UN chief 'deeply regrets' US visa refusal to Abbas for annual meeting
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres "deeply regrets" Washington's decision to deny a visa for the second year running to Palestinian leader Mahmoud Abbas, a UN spokesman said Friday, preventing him for attending the UN General Assembly.

data.title: Isolated Syrian-Druze city blames Damascus for shortages
data.description: SWEIDA (SYRIA) - In her bakery, Hoda Kiwan impatiently awaits flour and fuel, which have become scarce in southern Syria's Sweida, the Druze-majority city still outside Damascus' control.

data.title: Thailand's separatists vow to fight to the end
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR - Two decades into an insurgency that has killed thousands in southern Thailand, a leader of the main separatist group vowed this week to keep fighting until they achieve their goals.

data.title: Anthropic says AI systems moving towards building themselves
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO (UNITED STATES) - Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic said on Thursday that AI systems are increasingly capable of building future versions of themselves, adding to mounting concerns about the dangers of the powerful technology.

data.title: Athletes 'can't take it any more' as Asian Games issues mount
data.description: NAGOYA (JAPAN) - The Asian Games in Japan were on Friday facing more accusations of poor organisation with a world champion gymnast "totally exhausted", the public drafted in to rescue stranded athletes and South Korea lodging a complaint about a Japanese warlord.

data.title: Malaysian king allows jailed ex-PM Najib Razak to serve house arrest
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR - ‌Malaysia's king agreed on Friday to allow jailed former premier Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, the government said, four years after his conviction for his involvement in a multi-billion-dollar financial scandal.

data.title: Trump 'clearly' wants dialogue with Pyongyang: South Korean president
data.description: SEOUL - South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Friday that US President Donald Trump clearly wants dialogue with Pyongyang and confirmed Seoul will not be deploying troops to intervene militarily in the Iran war.

data.title: Thailand's Muslim separatists vow to fight to the end
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR - Two decades into an insurgency that has killed thousands in southern Thailand, a leader of the main Malay-Muslim separatist group vowed this week to keep fighting until they achieve their goals.

data.title: Afghan medical students in Pakistan hope court stops college expulsions
data.description: KARACHI - Dozens of Afghans studying to be doctors in Pakistan hope a court hearing on Friday will overturn an order by the country's medical board for them to be expelled from colleges and universities and sent home.

data.title: Australian athlete who soiled herself apologises for continuing Hyrox race
data.description: SYDNEY - An Australian athlete who sparked an outcry when she kept competing despite soiling herself midway through an event in Beijing apologised Friday and forfeited her points from winning.

data.title: Baby orangutans in India expose 'frightening' scale of trafficking
data.description: NEW DELHI - Five baby orangutans abandoned in an Indian forest have exposed a "massive" exotic wildlife trade, with traffickers smuggling increasingly rare species into the country, experts say.

data.title: Australia to detain tourists who overstay visa, minister says
data.description: SYDNEY - Australia has resolved to detain tourists who overstay visas to send a message of deterrence under new rules aimed at reducing levels of migration, a minister said on Friday.

data.title: English Championship rivals brace for renewal of bitter feuds
data.description: LONDON - Police are on red alert as the English Championship braces for the renewal of two bitter feuds when Millwall face West Ham and Wolves meet West Brom this weekend.

data.title: Bhutan's traditional archers lose ground to development
data.description: THIMPHU (BHUTAN) - Atop a steep hillside near Bhutan's capital Thimphu, an arrow slices through the air and slams into a wooden target with a thud, prompting a round of celebratory song.

data.title: Tokyo considers ordinance banning littering as downtown trash worsens
data.description: The Tokyo metropolitan government is considering an ordinance banning littering, as trash left in downtown entertainment districts has increased with the rise in tourists following the Covid-19 pandemic, government sources said on Thursday.

data.title: Mideast turmoil, AI set to dominate UN gathering of world leaders
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - As wars rage in the Middle East, Ukraine and Sudan, and fears mount over rapidly advancing AI, world leaders convened at the UN in New York for the world's signature diplomatic event.

data.title: Prized Mexican relic returns on loan, two centuries on
data.description: MEXICO CITY - A cherished 16th-century Mexican manuscript that tells the history of the Aztecs in pictograms went on display Thursday in Mexico City, nearly two centuries after it was whisked off to France.
